blocks.text: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), Hadhrat Abu Jahm (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) all Encourage Keeping to Oneself

Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) once said, "I wish I had someone to manage my finances so that I could lock my door and neither have anyone come to meet me nor go out to meet anyone until the day I meet Allaah." [^1]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Had it not been for the evil whisperings (of Shaytaan), I would go to a place where I have no friends (so that I could spend my time in solitude). It is only people who corrupt people." [^2]

Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed says that Hadhrat Abu Jahm bin Haarith bin Simma (RA) was a person who did not associate with his fellow Ansaar. When this solitude was mentioned to him, he remarked, "People are worse than solitude." [^3]

Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "The best monastery for a Muslim is his home where he is able to keep his carnal self his eyes and his private organs under control. Beware of the gatherings in the marketplaces because they involve a person in negligence and futile activities." [^4]
The Solitude of Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) once passed by Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) who was standing by his door and pointing with his fingers as if speaking to himself. "What is the matter, O Abu Abdur Rahmaan?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) asked, "Why are talking to yourself?" Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) replied, "What else can I do? That enemy of Allaah (Shaytaan) is trying to divert me from what I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say. He (Shaytaan) says, 'Why do you distress yourself by remaining at home all the time? Why do you rather not join the gatherings of people? I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that the person who goes out in the path of Allaah is in the guardianship of Allaah, the person who visits the ill is in the guardianship of Allaah, the person who goes morning or evening to the Masjid is in the guardianship of Allaah, the person who goes out to assist the (just) Muslim ruler is in the guardianship of Allaah and the person who stays at home without backbiting about anyone is in the guardianship of Allaah.' This enemy of Allaah wishes to take me out of my house to sit in the various gatherings of people." [^5]
Haakim, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.159). Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.278).
